chen: Heads up — saw linear mem growth in INT8 KV when serving very long contexts (>40k tokens). Accuracy delta vs fp16 starts showing up ~45k tokens (~1.6-1.9% perplexity regression). Profiling attached, dump below. Anyone seen similar? repro: `./run_infer --model redwood-7b-int8 --ctx 70000 --kv-mode paged --quant int8 --profile kv`

samir: Did you use QAT or post-train static quant?

chen: post-train static quant (no QAT). baseline is fp16. Telemetry shows eviction_count rising, fragmentation high. Kernel selection flips to `attention_generic` at certain sequence lengths which seems correlated.

maria: paste of the profiler output you mentioned?

chen: here — small excerpt from the profiling run:```
KV: pages_allocated=18
KV: pages_in_use=12
KV: fragmentation_pct=38
KV: eviction_count=214
KV: compactions=3
Kernel: chosen=attention_generic
Kernel: fallback_count=102
Batching: avg_batch_size=3.1
Batching: continuous_batching=true
Memory: rss_start=4.1G rss_end=8.7G
Accuracy: ppl_fp16=12.4 ppl_int8=12.6 (at 46k tokens)
```

aj: interesting — `attention_generic` is the scalar fallback we use on certain strides/sequence combos. It allocates intermediate buffers that are worse with int8 alignment. Could explain the RSS jump. Can you repro with `--kernel-debug` to log why kernel switch happened?

chen: yes will run with `--kernel-debug`. also noticed `kv.page_size=65536` and slot size is 48 bytes, so internal slack + alignment might blow up when quantized pages are slightly bigger.

maria: we've had a compaction edge-case before where free slots < threshold never triggered compaction for paged mode. quick patch we tried in another context:```c++
if (page.free_slots < COMPACT_THRESHOLD) compact_page(page);
```
Try setting `kv.compaction_policy=aggressive` or bump `kv.warmup_threshold` to 1024 and see if fragmentation drops.

chen: trying `kv.compaction_policy=aggressive` now on a canary pool. starting run.

infra-bot: profiling-job #pj-478 completed on canary (pool-canary-03). logs: https://internal.logs/pj-478

chen: canary run stats: fragmentation_pct down to 12, eviction_count ~18, rss_end 4.9G. accuracy still ~+1.4% vs fp16 though (improved). kernel still flips but fallback_count reduced.

samir: hmm partial win. Could still be quantization noise compounded by page warmup behavior. Do we have the model's quantization scale drift over long sequences? i.e., accumulating rounding error in KV when using int8 packing?

aj: theoretically int8 stores compressed keys/values so some precision loss in kv materialization is expected. But a 1-1.5% ppl delta at 45k tokens is higher than I've seen. Two hypotheses: (1) compaction/fragmentation causes extra copies that change alignment/rounding patterns, (2) kernel fallback path runs a slightly different math path (e.g., different softmax kernel) — both can amplify errors.

lisa: fwiw commit `abc1234` (PR #2987) touched the paged-kv allocator and introduced a new reserve routine. profiler indicates the first regressed deploy time matches that commit. @chen can you paste `git bisect` output?

chen: ran quick bisect, suspect range between `abc1000`..`abc1300`. `abc1234` is in the range and touches `reserve_page()` which changed how we mark free slots.

maria: if reserve_page changed bookkeeping, compaction might never see recently freed slots until later, that'd explain temporary fragmentation growth and extra evictions.

aj: plan: (A) run kernel-debug to record decision traces, (B) run exact same workload with `kv.compaction_policy=aggressive` + `kv.warmup_threshold=1024` vs `default`, (C) instrument quant rounding stats (mean abs diff of kv entries vs fp16) and (D) try repro with a deterministic mini-batch to rule out batching noise. I can take (A) and (D). @maria take (B)? @chen take (C) + bisect followup?

maria: taking (B). will spin two canaries and run side-by-side. setting `batching.max_delay_ms=2` to reduce batch variance.

lisa: I'll open a quick PR to revert `reserve_page` change to see if it's the culprit, and add more unit tests around compaction visibility. linking: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3021

chen: started instrument for quant rounding stats: will surface per-token kv residuals and aggregate. initial noisy run shows mean_abs_diff increasing slowly with sequence length. publishing results in ~30m.

infra-bot: canary runs queued: pj-479 (aggressive compaction) pj-480 (default). ETA ~25m.

samir: excellent. if we confirm bookkeeping bug, we should do a hotfix for Dedicated customers and schedule more thorough longctx suites in CI. also consider toggling model-side minimal QAT for a few models to test mitigation.

maria: quick note — if compaction/aggressive helps a lot, we need to watch perf CPU overhead. aggressive compaction increases CPU during steady-state. we'll measure CPU delta.

aj: true — tradeoff chart request: memory vs CPU vs latency. i'll add probes in the run.

chen: thanks all. will post the quant-residual graphs once done. action items: aj (kernel debug + deterministic mini-batch), maria (canary compaction A/B), chen (quant residuals + bisect), lisa (PR + tests). samir to coordinate customer impact comms if needed.

lisa: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: pj-479 started. logs: https://internal.logs/pj-479

chen: will follow up in thread with final numbers. thanks!
